tasks.title: Mass Balance
tasks.prompt: Feed is 100 t/h and gas outlet is 62 t/h. What must the liquid outlet be (t/h) for the balance to close?
tasks.tip: If a balance doesn't close, check the data.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.tip: Compare to the line sizing criterion.

tasks.title: Hydraulic Power
tasks.prompt: P = rho x g x Q x H. Density 1,000 kg/m³, Q 0.05 m³/s, head 40 m, g 9.81. What is power (kW)?
tasks.tip: Divide by efficiency for shaft power.
tasks.mistake: Quoting hydraulic power as motor size undersizes.

tasks.title: Layers of Protection
tasks.mistake: Counting the same device twice overstates safety.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: HAZOP Finding
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence HAZOP finding for 'no flow' to the separator.
tasks.modelAnswer: Deviation: no flow from the liquid outlet. Causes include a closed valve or pump trip; consequence is high level in the separator and liquid carry-over to the compressor. Safeguards: high-level alarm and a trip. Recommendation: confirm the trip is independent of the level controller and add a periodic proof test. Action owner: instrument engineer.
tasks.reasoning: A good HAZOP finding lists deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard and action.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Balance That Didn't Close
caseStudy.background: A project ignored a 6% mass balance gap. A flow meter was mis-scaled and the separator was undersized, requiring a costly retrofit.
caseStudy.challenges: The gap was dismissed as measurement noise.
caseStudy.solution: Hartmann requires balance closure within 2% before design freeze.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Don't design on data that doesn't close.
